a new blind frequency-offset synchronization algorithm for OFDM communications systems is developed.
a novel CFO estimation algorithm is proposed for OFDM systems with constant modulus modulations.

In summary, our research is concerned with
the design and analysis of a blind CFO estimation scheme for PSK-modulated OFDM signals.
the problem of carrier synchronization for OFDM communications systems.
the design of a blind frequency offset estimator for OFDM communications in a frequency selective fading channel.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the new blind estimator is superior to all existing blind techniques, both in performance and complexity.
the proposed CFO estimator achieves the same complexity as the existing VSC estimator, while providing a substantial performance gain.
the proposed CFO estimator outperforms the VSC-based estimator by 10 dB in SNR and one order of magnitude (i.e., 100 times) in MSE, and it is applicable to fully loaded systems.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we develop a new blind CFO synchronization technique that is highly accurate and computationally simple.
we have proposed an algorithm which is more accurate, more robust and more computationally efficient compared to the existing ones in the literature.
we have developed an algorithm for blind synchronization in OFDM systems that exploits the fact of constant modulus constellations and that it is consistent for fully loaded systems.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the Viterbi and Schilling criterion can be exploited to develop a highly accurate blind CFO estimator that is robust to frequency-selective fading and is consistent even for fully-loaded OFDM systems.
the VSC-based blind CFO estimator is sub-optimal and can be significantly improved.

, by exploiting the fact that OFDM signals are transmitted in blocks, we can achieve significant gains in performance, even when we have a very limited amount of information about the transmitted signal.
